This subject will remain relevant in the Church until Christ returns, because it is the one mission Christ entrusted to the Church. It is a great pity to see that so many people set this work aside to give themselves to useless controversies on subjects that do not affect salvation and sanctification in any way. We must rather concentrate on the essential, which is the salvation of souls.

But teaching evangelism is rather complex. To avoid getting lost, we will take an objective approach by looking at the example of the Lord himself, then that of the apostle Paul, whose path is fairly well traced in the Bible. After that, we will turn to the realities of our time to draw practical lessons.

1. The evangelism of our Lord

even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him. (Acts 10:38)

Jesus therefore said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and I do nothing of myself, but as my Father taught me, I say these things. He who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, for I always do the things that are pleasing to him.” (John 8:28-29)

Read also: John 5:17-20; John 7:16; John 12:49; John 14:14, 24.

Our Lord did not stay in place waiting for people to come. He went to look for them. He was in the habit of going to the synagogues, however. But he did not make uncontrolled movements. He followed the Father’s timing and went where the Father wanted him to go to do what the Father had planned. His key to determining what to do was prayer.

2. The apostle Paul and evangelism

Read Acts 13:4-5, 14-15, 42; Acts 16:12-13.

Led by the Holy Spirit, the apostle went from place to place, targeting especially the meeting places where people came to listen. These were then the centers of religion, philosophy, commerce, and so on. The apostle was not guided by his own calculations, he followed the Holy Spirit. He could know when the Spirit said no or yes (Acts 16:6-9). He prayed a lot and had companions who fought in prayer with him.

3. The situation of the millennium

  • Outside the places where Christ has not yet been mentioned, people claim to know Jesus. They believe they have nothing more to learn about the Christian religion. But they do not know the plan of salvation. That is what they must come to know.
  • The doctrines of Christianity are too numerous, and the different Christian denominations contradict one another. There are so many disputes in this religion that someone watching from afar may refuse to enter it. One must not talk doctrine with anyone before they give their life to Jesus Christ.
  • There are bad Christians and false pastors in the ranks of evangelicals. People know the stories or are even victims of them. One must honestly acknowledge the fact when it is brought up, and show that despite this God remains good and Jesus Christ is the only Savior.
  • The development of technology and the internet lets information travel faster. But it is also a road for poisoning against the gospel. Christians must quickly seize this means and saturate it with the truth of the gospel.
  • You must know the plan of salvation well and know how to present it with your own testimony through every means of communication available.

4. The plan of salvation and its presentation

a) Everyone is a sinner

Romans 3:23; Ecclesiastes 7:20; Isaiah 64:6; James 2:10

Presentation: God says that everyone is a sinner, I am, you are. Despite all morality, every man is a sinner. The good news is that God wants and is able to save all sinners. Besides, God cannot save a good person, because they will not want to be saved.

b) The penalty of sin is death (separation from God)

Romans 6:23; Isaiah 59:2; 2 Thessalonians 1:8-9; Revelation 20:14-15

Presentation: God loves us and he hates our sin because sin separates us from him. God does not want us to be separated from him.

c) Heaven (the dwelling of God) is a perfect place where only perfect people are admitted, that is, people without sin

2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:27; Psalm 5:4

Presentation: Heaven (paradise) is a perfect place. No sin can enter it because sin brings death.

d) Man cannot become perfect by himself

Ephesians 2:8-9; Romans 4:5; Galatians 2:16; Titus 3:5; Romans 3:28; Romans 11:6

Presentation: Man cannot do enough good to please God. He must accept what God has given him freely in Jesus Christ.

e) Christ has completely paid the ransom for our sins. He paid everything and offers us his righteousness

2 Corinthians 5:21; Isaiah 53:6; 1 Peter 3:18; 1 Peter 2:24; Colossians 2:13-14; Titus 2:14; Acts 13:38-39; Hebrews 10:10, 14; Romans 4:25

Presentation: Insist on the verses until the person understands that Jesus Christ paid everything.

f) All man has to do is believe that the Lord Jesus Christ paid for all sins and accept him as Savior

John 3:16; John 6:47; John 1:12; John 6:28-29; Ephesians 2:8; Romans 5:1, 8-11; Acts 13:38-39

Presentation: Do you believe that Jesus Christ paid for all sins, including yours?

g) We can be sure of having eternal life

Romans 6:23; John 3:16; John 6:47; 1 John 5:13

Presentation: Insist on the verses.

5. What should you say or not say?

When we are out evangelizing, it is normal to be careful to have the right words. For this we must know what we are in the Lord’s mind toward our non-believing listeners. We are the Lord’s messengers and his witnesses. A messenger says what he was ordered to say. A witness tells what he knows from having heard, seen, touched, or taken part in it. The witness tells his experience.

Two questions therefore emerge: What did Christ order us to say? And what is my experience with him?

Concerning what Jesus ordered us to say, we can read the following verses: Matthew 24:14; Mark 16:15.

The Lord wants us to announce the good news. The good news is that Jesus died for our sins, that he rose again and that he offers salvation to all who believe in him. Salvation is deliverance from the domination of Satan, from sin and from its punishment. Satan is the enemy of God and of his best creature, the human being. He is the author of all destruction. Sin originates from Satan. Sin is a cancer that eats away at the human being by deceiving him and leads him to a painful death. This death includes sufferings in this world and eternity in hell.

The solution to all this is already here, present in Jesus Christ, who paid the penalty of sin by his death on the cross, gave his blood to destroy the root of sin in the human being, and came back to life to ensure that those who accept him as Lord and Savior enjoy life fully here and afterward. That is what this means: The kingdom of heaven is near. All we have to do is acknowledge ourselves in a desperate situation, repent of our life without God, in sin, and accept eternal life (the fulfilled life) in Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ wants you to tell people this: The true, full and deep peace that you want inside and around you is now available. It is in God. To have it, return to God through Jesus Christ. You have nothing to pay.

But if you say this to someone, they may not believe you. Many so-called saviors have already made them enticing proposals that turned out to be deceptions. There are those who continue to hold them through interesting stratagems. And there is also the fact that many have already spoken of Jesus Christ without their seeing any real transformations. If they are to believe you, it will take more than your message. You must tell them what happened to you in the company of Jesus Christ. What did he do for you? This is where your personal testimony comes in.

6. Writing your testimony

Why? 1 Peter 3:15-16.

What is a testimony?

In a court of law, a testimony is a formal statement, written or oral, that proves an experience. As a Christian, your testimony is similar. It is an account of what God has done in your life and how you came to know and follow him through those experiences. Your testimony is your story of God. Sharing personal experiences of how Jesus transformed your life will always have more impact than an impersonal, general statement of faith.

A good testimony should explain:

a) WHAT your life was like BEFORE you decided to follow Jesus

You can answer questions like:

  • What was my life really like? (Lonely, empty, shallow, etc.)
  • What marked me most in my life? (Work, a partner, alcohol, etc.)
  • Where did I get my security or happiness? (Success, possessions, etc.)
  • How did these things begin to disappoint me?

b) WHY you decided to follow Jesus

You can answer questions like:

  • When did I first hear about the Gospel or about Jesus?
  • What were my first reactions?
  • When did my attitude begin to change? Why?
  • What were the last struggles that went through my mind before I accepted Jesus?
  • Why did I accept Jesus?

c) HOW your life changed after Jesus

Write a sentence or two on each of these points:

  • How did this experience change your perspective on God and on life?
  • Describe how it has impacted the way you live, feel and think.
  • How has this story changed the way you see and understand God?

This is the part that has the most impact, because now you are presenting a vision of God based on things you have actually experienced.

Keep your language simple

Words like sin, salvation, fellowship, sanctification and gospel can leave non-believers confused or even disgusted, because they do not really understand them. It is even possible that many Christians who use them do not know much about them either. If you use such words, try to replace them with commonly used expressions. Instead of using a phrase like “my sins are washed away by the blood”, try saying something like “Jesus forgave the things I did wrong, and gave me a fresh start”. That does not mean the first expression is wrong, but people are simply not familiar with this “Christian” language.

Stick to the essentials

Define a theme and focus on it. What is the key notion of your life that is relevant to people who do not know God? What did Jesus really change in your life? What were you like before Jesus entered your life? What are you like now thanks to friendship with Jesus? If you have been a Christian since childhood, what experience stands out in your walk with Christ?

Praying for the sick should not be complicated. But the mystery people make of spirituality complicates this matter which is meant to be simple. It should be noted that praying for the healing of a sick person is different from what is called deliverance today. In that case, we refer to driving an evil spirit out of a person who is possessed by it. There is much to say and explain on this subject.

In a sense, every healing is a deliverance. Sickness is a result of sin. This does not mean that all those who are sick became so because of committing a particular sin. Sickness, like all the other disorders we have in creation, is the result of original sin. And sin originates in the rebellion orchestrated by the devil. Every infirmity is therefore a direct or indirect action of the devil. Performing a healing is therefore delivering the sick person from his oppressor. Whatever the opinions and theories on the origin and cause of sickness, the administration and obtaining of healing follow the same process clearly explained in the Scriptures.

1. Taking your own healing

Let us explain with the example of the woman who suffered from bleeding for twelve years (Matthew 9:20-22).

There were 3 steps in the miracle described:

  • First, the woman heard about Jesus Christ.
  • Second, the woman believed in him.
  • Third, the woman walked by her faith.

Every Christian knows God’s power and will to heal him and guarantee him divine health. God does not only want to heal us, he has already done it in Jesus Christ. It is a fact. This knowledge must be turned into conviction. He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds. (1 Pet 2:24) There is no reason for God to strike you with sickness and want to kill you with it. His promise is quite different: You shall serve Yahweh your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will take sickness away from among you. (Exod 23:25)

Even if there is a sin, forgiveness is with God. If we humble ourselves under God’s hand, acknowledging our wrongs, God promises to restore us and keep us in good health (2 Chronicles 7:14). That is why, whatever pathologies we may find ourselves subject to, we must believe in God for our healing.

Next, we must touch the Lord by using the promises God made that relate to healing. We must take these biblical words, confess them and declare them over ourselves. We must use our authority. We have authority over our own body. We must use this authority and command the sickness to leave our body and to stay far away.

Finally, we must believe that God did what he promised and act accordingly. Make an effort to do movements you could not do and keep the confession of your healing. The devil may try to deceive you by bringing back the symptoms of the sickness. Refuse to give him access. Tell him that you are healed and will stay so. Tell him that you believe the Word of God and not the symptoms. Thank God for your healing. Above all, do not ask for healing anymore. You are already healed.

2. Administering healing

This concerns a sick person who is unable to take healing for himself. It may be a new convert who has not yet had teachings on faith. It may also be a person too weakened by the illness or a person who feels accused by his conscience and therefore has no assurance before God. What the Bible says in this case is in James 5:14-15.

The Bible says to call the elders. Why the elders? The sick person who doubts himself before God can have faith to be healed only in the presence of a person whose relationship with God he believes to be in good standing and developed enough to attract God’s favor upon him.

Normally, the healing ministry is a privilege of all believers. All who believe in Christ can lay hands on the sick and the sick will be healed (Mark 16:17). These are the very words of our Lord Jesus Christ. No doubt is attached to them. So in place of the word elder, one can very well put “a brother or sister in the faith”.

These must first have the sick person confess his sins. They must pray for his forgiveness and receive it by faith.

Next, they must bring the sick person to confess the biblical promises as far as possible.

Finally, they must lay hands on him and anoint him with oil if present. During the laying on of hands, they must pray, imploring God’s grace, commanding the evil out, and declaring the sick person healed in the name of Jesus Christ. If a person is gifted by the Holy Spirit with the gift of healing or working of miracles, the healing ministry would be easier for him.

In summary, you arrive somewhere where there is a sick person asking for prayer. You approach with compassion and speak to the sick person. Say for example: “God loves you and the healing that is found in Jesus Christ will manifest in your body.” Then you ask whether his conscience is at peace. Does he feel accused of anything? If so, he confesses and you help him receive forgiveness by faith. If he is an unbeliever, you lead him to faith in Christ. Finally, you lay hands on him and pray, declaring him healed. (If you have olive oil, put some on your hands before laying them on the sick person. However, this is not indispensable.)

We are of the opinion that prevention is better than cure. A child of God must prefer to live in good health rather than fall sick and receive healing each time. Although healing is the children’s bread and our God is Jehovah Rapha, that is, the God who heals, it is appropriate to advocate being in good health rather than regularly receiving healing. To do this, we recommend that God’s children understand and respect the principles for being in good health. (See the module “Mastering your health and your money”)

As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’ Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give. (Matt 10:7-8)

By saying “cast out demons”, the Lord Jesus Christ established the operation we mean by deliverance. Moreover, he practiced it on several people. In addition, it is a doctrine belonging entirely and exclusively to the new covenant in Jesus Christ. Indeed, the first time people saw Jesus Christ practice deliverance, Amazement came on all, and they spoke together, one with another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!” (Luke 4:36)

It was astonishing to them because the old covenant offered no solution for people possessed by unclean spirits. They were lost causes. They had to be eliminated physically so that they would not contaminate the rest of the people. But the Son of God, Jesus Christ our Lord, came not to destroy men’s souls, but to save them (Luke 9:56). He also gave himself the mission of destroying the works of the evil one (1 John 3:8).

Deliverance consists of destroying the works of the evil one in a person. It will be a matter of dethroning the spirit that has sat in the person, driving it out of the person’s spirit, soul and body. It will be a matter of completely destroying its establishment in this person. It will finally be a matter of restoring the person to his original image. Thus, deliverance has several levels, just as the control of an evil spirit over a person has different levels.

1. Oppression

When a demon acts from a distance on a person’s body, it is oppression. This results in an incomprehensible illness that defies medicine. Sometimes, it may well be a known illness that resists treatment. This person does not need deliverance. He needs healing. He can take it by his own faith or with the help of a brother or through the ministry of a person with the gift of healings or working of miracles.

2. Temptation

When the demon, from the outside, inspires ungodly desires or negative thoughts such as uncontrolled carnal desire, inferiority complex, rage, the desire for suicide, or fear of death or of unhappy events, we are in the presence of temptation. Before the demon had this access, the man must have made the way for him through covetousness, anger, bitterness, etc.

One must therefore submit to God by confessing one’s sins, and resist the devil by expressing outwardly one’s decision to remain in the love of God, to walk in faith and to live the will of God. This can be done alone or with the help of a brother or sister mature in the faith. The need for help arises when one already sees oneself at an impasse.

3. Obsession

If temptation is accepted, the demon can take possession of the person’s soul. A person accepts temptation when he spends too much time pondering negative thoughts and especially if he acts accordingly. If a person continues to think that he is nothing even though the Holy Spirit reminds him of God’s love, he quenches the Holy Spirit and opens the door of his soul to the demon of inferiority complex. The latter will bring rage, the desire for revenge. Seeing himself unable to satisfy his unhealthy desires, the soul will desire death. The place is well prepared and any spirit can settle in. This is obsession.

When desires for something forbidden by the Word of God take hold, obsession comes quite quickly. One can get rid of it personally at its primary stage, because until then one has control. Obsession begins with suffering inside, not for some ailment, but because of this unsatisfied desire. It hurts. The more it hurts, the more one lets oneself be bound in his will by the demon.

To get rid of obsession, one must accept the Word of God. The operation of this sword will also cause pain. God will not coddle us. He will not tell you: “it’s all right, I understand…” On the contrary, he will call you to correct your ways. He will call you to order. He will make you see your fault. You will feel abandoned because it is you whom the word condemns first. The sword will go all the way to your joints and marrow, to extract the venom. It will not spare your eye. It will pull on the beam until it removes it. If you let yourself go through the operation, humbling yourself under God’s hand, your healing will quickly sprout.

The key is this: Accept your wrong! And leave it to God to justify you! (Romans 12:18-21) It is always good at this level to ask, if possible, for the help of an elder in the faith.

Advanced obsession

The advanced level of obsession is where the person no longer controls himself. Indeed, obsession can be advanced to the point that the individual begins to act like a person completely out of his senses. A lunatic, a person who communicates with imaginary beings, may simply be under obsession. The frenzied movements of an obsessed person often occur when he is in the presence of the anointing of the Holy Spirit. That is why people come in full possession of their senses to a prayer meeting and soon start doing and saying things one could never have suspected of them. This means that many of their actions, even when they seemed perfectly sensible, were in reality of demonic origin.

What to do in such cases? You must firmly order the spirit to come out in the name of Jesus Christ. You must stay firm. You must not shout or waste time looking for Bible verses that might work. It is no use saying to a demon that obsesses a person: “it is written…” You must simply command it to come out in the name of Jesus Christ. It will not resist. It knows that to Jesus Christ our Lord has been given the name that is above every name (Philippians 2:9-11).

So do not doubt and do not ask yourself whether you have the right words. Do not ask yourself whether you have the anointing and the authority. You have them! Jesus Christ said: “These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons …” (Mark 16:17) Do you believe in Jesus Christ? Is he your Lord and Savior? Can you cast out demons?

When the person has regained his calm, it is necessary to work more with him, in order to root him in the Word and thus close the door to the demons that were obsessing him.

4. Possession

Possession is the most advanced case of demonic operation in an individual. The evil spirit then has control of the spirit of the man in question. This can never happen to a born-again Christian, because his born-again spirit is inhabited by the Holy Spirit. “That which is born of the Spirit is spirit” (John 3:6). And “he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit” (1 Corinthians 6:17).

This being so, the demon cannot lodge in the born-again spirit of a child of God. Possession can only be the case of an unbeliever. The manifestations may resemble advanced obsession and go further. It must be said that the devil can possess a person and nevertheless leave him control of his senses. This is generally the case with sorcerers and occultists. There are even apparently simple people who are in this case. Prostitutes, bandits, terrorists are in the same case. Among politicians, the possessed are many. It would be rare to find an unbelieving man who is not possessed. That is why the few cases of spectacular deliverances should not make us believe that the others are fine. In reality, “the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the Good News of the glory of Christ … should not dawn on them” (2 Corinthians 4:4).

We must therefore begin this ministry of deliverance with intercession. Let us pray that God opens their eyes so that they see the splendor of the Gospel and accept it. Indeed, from that moment, the Holy Spirit positions himself in the man’s spirit, breaking the devil’s power over him. Conversion is the greatest deliverance. That is also why, in addition to intercession, we must spread in every layer of society the Word of grace, of love and of salvation of our God and Savior Jesus Christ, who wants all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4).

Faced with a case of possession where the individual does not have his senses, what must we do? We must act following the example of our Lord Jesus Christ, who drives out demons with his Word (Matthew 8:16). You must firmly command the spirit to come out in the name of Jesus Christ. You must reduce conversation with demons to the minimum. Their nature is to lie. If you believe them, they can lead you into error. You must simply drive the demon out of this ground that he thinks is his, close the door and establish the reign of God by the Holy Spirit. Everything must be done in the name of Jesus Christ. One can declare Bible verses, but one must not make an esoteric recitation of them. And one must at all costs avoid using words, names and expressions that are against the sound doctrine of the Word of God.

This module is the module of the outward mission. After all the inner work of the previous modules, it is now time to go toward others. The Builder does not keep the good news to himself.

“Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.” (Matt 10:8)

The plan of salvation in 7 points

Know these 7 points by heart. You can present them to anyone, anywhere, in 5 minutes.

Everyone is a sinner — Rom 3:23

God says that everyone is a sinner — you and me. Despite all morality, every man is a sinner. The good news: God can save all sinners.

The penalty of sin is death — Rom 6:23

Sin separates us from God (spiritual death). God loves us and hates our sin because sin separates us from him.

Heaven admits only perfect people — Rev 21:27

Paradise is a perfect place. No sin can enter it. Man is incapable of making himself perfect by himself.

Man cannot save himself — Eph 2:8-9

Man cannot do enough good to please God. He must accept what God gives him freely in Christ.

Christ paid everything — 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 2:24

Jesus Christ paid the complete penalty of sin. His blood covered everything. Nothing remains to be paid.

You must believe and accept Christ — John 3:16; John 1:12

Do you believe that Jesus Christ paid for all your sins? Accept him as Lord and Savior — that is all.

You can be sure of having eternal life — 1 John 5:13

Eternal life is not a vague promise — it is a certainty for the one who believes in Jesus Christ.

What you say to someone who does not know God:

“The true, full and deep peace that you want inside and around you is now available. It is in God. To have it, return to God through Jesus Christ. You have nothing to pay.”

Healing: 2 situations, 2 approaches

Taking your own healing

1. Hear: know the promises of healing

2. Believe: turn knowledge into conviction

3. Act: confess your healing and make the impossible movements

4. Hold on: refuse the symptoms, give thanks

Administering healing

1. Have the sick person confess sins, pray for forgiveness

2. Bring the sick person to confess the biblical promises

3. Lay on hands (+ olive oil if available)

4. Command the evil out, declare the sick person healed

Every believer in Christ can pray for the sick. It is not reserved for pastors. Mark 16:17-18 is clear: “those who believe”. Have you believed? You can pray.

Deliverance: 4 levels of demonic operation

It is crucial to identify the level correctly in order to give the right response.

Level 1: Oppression

The demon acts from a distance on the body. Result: unexplained sickness that defies medicine. Response: prayer for healing, not deliverance.

Level 2: Temptation

The demon inspires from the outside ungodly thoughts or negative desires. Response: submit to God, confess your sins, resist the devil firmly.

Level 3: Obsession

The demon takes possession of the soul. The person begins to lose control of his actions. Response: accept the Word of God, humble yourself, command the spirit to come out in the name of Jesus.

Level 4: Possession

The demon controls the spirit. CANNOT happen to a born-again Christian. Response: firmly command the spirit to come out in the name of Jesus Christ.

Do not ask yourself whether you have the right words, the anointing, the authority. You have them! Do you believe in Jesus Christ? Then you can cast out demons (Mark 16:17).

objectifs: You know the plan of salvation and can present it simply in 5 minutes.
You have written your structured personal testimony and you use it to evangelize.
You know how to pray for the sick with confidence — without wondering whether you are spiritual enough.
You know the 4 levels of demonic operation and how to respond to each.

qcm.q: What does Matthew 10:7-8 say to the disciples?
c: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out demons: freely you received, freely give
qcm.e: This is the module of the outward mission: the Builder does not keep the good news to himself.

qcm.q: What is the difference between a messenger and a witness?
c: The messenger says what he was ordered to say; the witness tells his experience
qcm.e: Two questions: what did Christ order us to say? What is my experience with him?

qcm.q: What must you not do with a listener before he gives his life to Jesus Christ?
qcm.e: Doctrines are many and denominations contradict one another: we begin with the plan of salvation.

qcm.q: What does “salvation” mean, according to the module?
c: Deliverance from the domination of Satan, from sin and from its punishment
qcm.e: Jesus paid the penalty of sin by his death on the cross.

qcm.q: What can you do to be sure of having eternal life, according to the plan of salvation presented?
c: Belong to the right Christian denomination
Believe that Jesus Christ paid for all sins and accept him as Savior
Do enough good works to please God
Wait until the end of your life to be judged
qcm.e: Ephesians 2:8-9: man cannot become perfect by himself; he must accept what God gives freely in Jesus Christ.

qcm.q: What is the first point of the plan of salvation, according to Romans 3:23?
qcm.e: Despite all morality, every man is a sinner; God can save all sinners.

qcm.q: A good testimony has three parts: which ones?
qcm.e: What my life was like before, why I decided to follow Jesus, what Christ changed.

qcm.q: What are the three steps of the woman with the flow of blood (Matthew 9:20-22)?
c: She heard about Jesus, she believed in him, she walked by her faith
qcm.e: Hear, believe, act: this is the path for taking your own healing.

qcm.q: What are the four steps for administering healing to a sick person?
c: Ask questions, give advice, leave, forget
Have him confess sins and pray for forgiveness; bring him to confess the biblical promises; lay on hands (olive oil if available); command the evil out and declare the sick person healed
qcm.e: It is a simple path, not a mystery.

qcm.q: Who can pray for the sick, according to Mark 16:17-18?
c: Those who have believed: every believer in Christ
qcm.e: “Those who believe”: have you believed? You can pray.

qcm.q: What are the four levels of demonic operation?
qcm.e: It is crucial to identify the level in order to give the right response.

qcm.q: What is temptation, as a level of demonic operation?
c: A simple bad dream of no importance
An unexplained illness that defies medicine
A demon already lives in the person
The demon inspires ungodly desires or negative thoughts from the outside, and it is resisted by submitting to God
qcm.e: We confess our sins, submit to God and resist the devil. We can ask for the help of a brother or sister mature in the faith (James 4:7).

qcm.q: What is the response to the level of oppression (unexplained illness that defies medicine)?
qcm.e: The demon acts from a distance on the body.

qcm.q: How do you get rid of obsession, according to the module?
c: By accepting the Word of God, even if its operation hurts, and correcting your ways
By waiting for it to pass by itself
By letting the demon settle in so that he gets tired
qcm.e: Obsession begins with a suffering due to unsatisfied desire. At its primary stage, you can get rid of it personally.

qcm.q: What does the module say about possession?
c: It cannot happen to a born-again Christian, whose spirit is inhabited by the Holy Spirit
It happens easily to a believer

exercices.consigne: With your partner, your neighbor or a trusted person, one plays the role of the evangelist, the other that of the non-believer. Present the 7 points in 5 minutes maximum. Then switch roles. If you are alone, present them aloud as if someone were listening.

exercices.consigne: A good testimony has 3 parts. Write yours here; you will summarize it in the sheet (300 words maximum).
